text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Iraq defies United Nations Gulf War resolutions with flight to Jeddah. Iraq flew 104 Moslem pilgrims to Saudi Arabia on Wednesday despite a U.N.-imposed embargo against Baghdad since its 1990-91 occupation of Kuwait.

- Kuwait's foreign reserves show record improvement, Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan says. Kuwait's foreign investments portfolio, once estimated at $100 billion, fell to around $40 billion, mainly due to the costs of the 1991 Gulf War that ended Iraq's seven month occupation and reconstruction costs.
- Fifteen-year-old studnet shoots teacher over expulsion.

- New mobile telecommunications firm to be established in October, official says. Mobile Telecommunications Company is currently the sole provider of mobile telephone services in the Gulf Arab state of two million people.

- Polypropylene plant to be operational in four months, says official at the state-owned Petrochemical Industries Company (PIC). The plant is expected to produce 100,000 tonnes per year of polypropylene.
- Parliamentrian proposes ban on import of Jordanian vegetables and fruits. Kuwaitis accuse Jordanians of sympathising with Baghdad during its occupation of Kuwait.

- Foreign residents to be obliged to pay health insurance fees as of 1998. The state offers health care free of charge for Kuwaitis. It imposes charges on selected services for its 1.2 million foreign residents.
